label: Universal suffrage introduction year
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = a curated table of dated franchise introductions (16 countries, 1848-1946, one citation per point — the standard scholarly dating of the Caramani electoral-archive family, the male/female decomposition carried per row in definition_note); no witness tier exists (no machine-readable door carries the series — probed live 2026-09-20).

notes:
THE ELEVENTH INDICATOR, THE SECOND MARKER (v15). Todd's L'invention de l'Europe (1990, 7 citations) reads the introduction of universal suffrage as the anthropological fingerprint: the exogamous communal systems of Western Europe universalized the vote EARLY and from below (France 1848, Germany 1871), the authoritarian-family belt late and from above (Austria 1907, Belgium 1919 — the plural-vote compromise dissolving only then), the asymmetric-communal north splitting the date in two (Sweden's '1911/1921', the corpus label's own dual dating: the male grant and the female grant a decade apart). The marker dates the franchise's arrival as the historiography dates it — which for the 19th-century introductions IS the male grant (they were called 'suffrage universel' at the time, women's exclusion notwithstanding) and for the later ones the completing women's grant (Norway 1913, Denmark 1915, the Netherlands 1919). The male/female decomposition rides EVERY row's definition_note: Todd's own convention (he prints '1911/1921' for Sweden), applied uniformly.
THE MARKER'S SHAPE: one point per country, the point's year = the introduction year, the value = the same year (the board reads the STEP: France 1848, Austria 1907, Italy 1946 — Catholic Europe's late completion, the family-systems map's own order). Every point carries its citation (the standard scholarly dating, the Caramani electoral- archive family) and its decomposition note (e.g. Switzerland: male 1848, women 1971 — the famous latecomer the Catholic-periphery argument reads).
THE CURATION GATE (ADR-0007, all three conditions): (a) the todd_ref demands it — 7 citations in L'invention de l'Europe, the book's comparative-anthropology core; (b) the distortion is the ABSENCE — no door carries the series (probed live, the OWID candidate slugs all 404, electoral history lives in print archives); (c) every row carries its citation — enforced mechanically.
HONEST SCOPE LIMITS: 16 countries = Todd's own named set (Sweden, Austria, Belgium, the UK, Norway) extended to the European core his maps compare against (the founding six + the Nordic pair + the Catholic pair + the latecomers Italy and Switzerland); the countries outside the European comparison set have NO row (the honest absent state); the dating CONVENTION itself (male grant vs women's completion) is the one interpretive choice, and it rides every row's note rather than hiding in a footnote — as-reported, where 'as' is 'as the historiography that Todd cites'.
